messages.content: Complete the following case-report text from the exact point where it stops. Return only the most likely original continuation, without repeating the supplied text, adding headings, quoting the prompt, or explaining your approach. This is a text-continuation task. Write up to 125 whitespace-separated words.

A 54-year-old male was sent to the emergency department (ED) within 30 min of being found unresponsive at a health spa. His medical history was limited to treated hepatitis C and a remote appendectomy, with no known chronic illnesses or regular medication use. Upon arrival, his vital signs were notable for relative hypotension (104/58 mmHg), bradypnea (12 breaths/min), and hypothermia (34.3 °C), with a Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score of E3V2M5. Physical examination revealed a state of flaccid paralysis with generalized areflexia, including absent deep tendon reflexes. Laboratory screening for common drugs of abuse was negative. Initial blood samples obtained after ED arrival showed blood urea nitrogen and serum creatinine concentrations of 14 and 0.9 mg/dL, respectively. Arterial blood gas analysis demonstrated mixed respiratory and

message.content: metabolic acidosis with a pH of 7.28, PaCO2 of 58 mmHg, and HCO3 of 22 mEq/L. Serum electrolytes, liver function tests, and complete blood count were within normal limits. Given the constellation of descending flaccid paralysis, areflexia, and respiratory compromise in the absence of a toxicological explanation, botulism was strongly suspected. The patient was intubated for airway protection and mechanical ventilation. Stool and serum samples were sent for botulinum toxin testing. He was admitted to the intensive care unit and received heptavalent botulinum antitoxin. Over the following days, his respiratory function gradually improved, and he was extubated on day 4. Full neurological recovery was observed over several weeks, and toxin testing confirmed the diagnosis of foodborne botulism.
